answer: A durable defense is collateral-backed identity with slashing. Each agent locks a deposit that grows with the privileges it claims, like a dune that only holds its shape while grains keep arriving. A newcomer starts with narrow rights on the tundra edge of the network; every verified, useful job slowly raises its limit, while a single proven fraud burns part of the stake and freezes the account. Creating a hundred hollow identities then costs a hundred deposits, and one bad act can wipe out the whole pile, so honest work becomes far cheaper than running a fake army.
